description: Understand the fundamental concepts, methodologies, and applications of Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) for solving complex decision-making problems. Apply full aggregation, outranking, and reference-level approaches to evaluate, rank, and select alternatives based on multiple decision criteria. Analyze and compare different MCDA techniques to identify appropriate decision-making methods for diverse engineering and real-world applications. Develop decision-support solutions using optimization techniques, integrated MCDA systems, and software tools for multi-criteria decision problems. Demonstrate the application of MCDA methods in engineering, business, healthcare, supply chain, and other multidisciplinary domains.

syllabus.title: General Introduction
syllabus.body: Introduction, decision problems, MCDA methods and software, selection of MCDA methods, choice, ranking, sorting and description problems, applications of MCDA.

syllabus.title: Full Aggregation Approach
syllabus.body: Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP): problem structuring, priority calculation, consistency check, sensitivity analysis, extensions; Analytic Network Process (ANP): inner/outer dependency, influence matrix, supermatrix; Multi-Attribute Utility Theory (MAUT): additive model, utility functions; UTA method, MACBETH, value tree, score calculation, robustness analysis.

syllabus.title: Outranking Approach
syllabus.body: PROMETHEE: unicriterion preference degrees, positive/negative/net flows, GAIA plane, sensitivity analysis, PROMETHEE I and II ranking; ELECTRE: outranking relations, partial/global concordance and discordance degree, outranking degree, partial ranking, ELECTRE-Tri.

syllabus.title: Goal, Aspiration or Reference-Level Approach and Integrated Systems
syllabus.body: TOPSIS: ideal and anti-ideal solution, separation measures, relative closeness; Goal Programming: weighted, lexicographic, Chebyshev; Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA): efficiency measurement, constant and variable returns to scale, sensitivity analysis; multi-method platforms, GIS, group decision support systems, applications of MCDA.

outcomes: Explain the principles, classifications, and applications of MCDA and identify appropriate methods for different decision-making scenarios.
Apply full aggregation methods such as AHP, ANP, MAUT, UTA, and MACBETH to structure decision problems and evaluate alternatives.
Analyze and compare alternatives using outranking methods such as PROMETHEE and ELECTRE.
Evaluate decision alternatives using reference-level approaches, including TOPSIS, Goal Programming, and DEA.
Design and implement decision support models by integrating MCDA methods with software tools for real-world decision-making problems.
textbooks: Alessio Ishizaka and Philippe Nemery, Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis: Methods and Software, Wiley, 2013.
Zilany, Milan, Multi Criteria Decision Making, McGraw Hill Book Company, 1982.
referenceBooks: R. Steuer, Multiple Criteria Optimization: Theory, Computation and Application, John Wiley & Sons, 1985.
Ching-Lai Hwang and Kwangsun Yoon, Multiple Attribute Decision Making: Methods and Applications, Springer.
